newsitem.title: UK: British government plans to end lottery profits.
newsitem.headline: British government plans to end lottery profits.

text.p: Britain's new Labour government plans to push ahead immediately with diverting cash from the national lottery to health and education projects and to eventually end the lottery's profit-making status, the Financial Times said on Friday.
National Heritage Secretary Chris Smith was quoted as saying he was determined to create a non-profit-making lottery when the current licence expired in November 2001.
The Financial Times said the news would come as a blow to Camelot, the operator, which had hoped to bid for a new licence.

Camelot makes just under one penny in the pound, or one percent, profit from turnover of the lottery -- which is drawn on Wednesdays and Saturdays -- and has become more profitable more quickly than expected.
